description: Create src/targets/base.js: the formal discovery target-adapter interface (JSDoc @typedefs) plus a ProvisioningAdapter base class that owns the generic git/compose/docker/sql/cleanup provisioning machinery extracted (behavior-unchanged) from DadAdapter in src/dad.js. This is the reusable foundation FEAT-002 builds on; it wires no adapter yet and changes no existing file, so the tree stays green. Grounded in src/dad.js read in full. Independent of FEAT-002's relocations except that FEAT-002 depends on this file existing.
steps: Create src/targets/base.js. At the top add a JSDoc @typedef block documenting the formal interface per design §1: Actor { id, description, entry, cookie?, cookieName? }; Fixture { replay?(), inspect?() }; and the adapter contract (required snapshot/docker/build/database/deploy/discoveryFixture/cleanup + publicOrigin/signal; optional discoveryReplayFixture/source). Include fold-in #5 as a comment: the discovery-phase evidence (discovery.json, discovery-trace.zip) and acceptance-only journey evidence are produced by the RUNNER/engine, not the adapter — the adapter owns only the five provisioning phases' evidence (candidate.json; docker.log,compose-version.log; build-api.log,build-web.log; migrations.log,test-migrations.log; readiness.log) plus cleanup.log.

Define `export class ProvisioningAdapter`. Base constructor sets this.run, this.id = run.data.id, this.signal, this.created = false (DAD's subclass constructor sets repo/revision/sourceIdentity/source/file and calls super or sets the base fields — FEAT-002 handles the DAD constructor).

Add `freePort()` as a base METHOD (fold-in #3 decision) with the exact body currently at src/dad.js:12-21 (createServer, listen(0,'127.0.0.1'), read port, close). It is called as this.freePort() by the DAD subclass in FEAT-002. Mechanical symbol-resolution change, no behavioral effect.

Move `logged(result, label, binary, args, options = {})` verbatim from src/dad.js (writes `${label}.log` evidence on both success via output.stdout+output.stderr and failure via error.stdout+error.stderr+message, then rethrows). Imports: `import { command } from '../process.js';`.

Add the NEW helper `composeRun(result, label, args, options)` that returns `this.logged(result, label, 'docker', ['compose','-p',this.id,'-f',this.file, ...args], options)` — prepends EXACTLY those four elements then appends args verbatim.

Add the NEW helper `execSql({ service, user, db }, query)` that returns `this.compose(['exec','-T',service,'psql','-X','-v','ON_ERROR_STOP=1','-U',user,'-d',db,'-At'], { input: query })`. Only service/user/db are parameterized; `-X -v ON_ERROR_STOP=1` are load-bearing and must not be dropped or reordered.

Move the generic git-archive snapshot skeleton (rev-parse verify + hex regex, .env refusal, ls-tree, git archive -> tar -x into this.source, sourceArchiveSha256 via digest, diff-tree/status candidate bookkeeping) into base, with the DAD required-files list passed IN by the caller (not hardcoded). Keep behavior identical; the DAD-specific required-files array stays in FEAT-002's config. If a clean generic extraction risks changing DAD bytes, keep snapshot logic in the DAD subclass instead and note it in findings — byte-identity wins over extraction purity.

Move the image build+inspect loop shape (build [service,dockerfile] pairs then `docker image inspect --format {{.Id}}`) into a base helper that takes an already-resolved service/dockerfile/build-arg list. The mode-conditional *-checks branching stays in DAD (FEAT-002), NOT in this helper.

Move the compose up/down lifecycle wrappers and the generic cleanup flow (best-effort tail-log collection via compose(['logs',...]) swallowing errors, then composeRun down --volumes --remove-orphans --timeout 10 with { timeout: 90_000 }, else write the no-op cleanup.log). The service list for log collection is passed in by DAD.

Create test/base.test.js: (a) `logged` writes `${label}.log` on success AND on failure, using a fake command (inject or monkeypatch) and an in-memory run.evidence collector; (b) `composeRun` prepends exactly ['compose','-p',id,'-f',file] and appends args verbatim (capture via a stubbed logged/command); (c) `execSql` emits ['compose','-p',id,'-f',file,'exec','-T',service,'psql','-X','-v','ON_ERROR_STOP=1','-U',user,'-d',db,'-At'] for given service/user/db.

Run `npm run lint` and `npm test`; fix any issue. Commit locally on feat/adapter-interface (e.g. `git -C /Users/shawncoe/Documents/dev/DAD/atm/.worktrees/move3-adapter-split add src/targets/base.js test/base.test.js && git -C ... commit -m 'refactor: add ProvisioningAdapter base + formal interface'`). Never push.
acceptance_criteria: src/targets/base.js exists exporting `ProvisioningAdapter` with methods freePort, logged, compose, composeRun, execSql, the snapshot/build/cleanup generic helpers, and the @typedef interface docs.
No existing src/ file is modified by this feature (base.js and test/base.test.js are additions only).
`npm test` is fully green, including the new test/base.test.js cases for logged/composeRun/execSql.
composeRun prepends exactly ['compose','-p',id,'-f',file]; execSql pins ['exec','-T',service,'psql','-X','-v','ON_ERROR_STOP=1','-U',user,'-d',db,'-At'] — proven by base.test.js.
findings:
Done. src/targets/base.js created; no existing src/ file touched. Baseline 109 -> 113 pass, lint clean.

EXPORTED SYMBOLS FEAT-002 must bind to:
- `export class ProvisioningAdapter` (named export, from '../targets/base.js' relative to src/targets/dad/index.js use '../base.js'). It is the ONLY export of base.js. The @typedefs (Actor, Fixture, DiscoveryTargetAdapter) are JSDoc-only, not runtime exports.
- Constructor: `new ProvisioningAdapter(run)` sets this.run, this.id = run.data.id, this.signal = undefined, this.created = false. It does NOT set repo/revision/source/file. DAD's subclass constructor must call `super(run)` then set this.repo, this.revision, this.sourceIdentity, this.source, this.file itself (matching the current DadAdapter constructor body). Note the base constructor takes ONLY `run` (single arg) — the DAD options object ({repo,revision,sourceIdentity,signal}) is handled entirely in the DAD subclass.

Base methods available to the DAD subclass:
- `freePort()` — async base METHOD (fold-in #3). DAD build/docker call site becomes `await this.freePort()`.
- `logged(result, label, binary, args, options = {})` — verbatim move; writes `${label}.log` on success and failure, rethrows.
- `compose(args, options = {})` — verbatim; prepends ['compose','-p',this.id,'-f',this.file]. deploy readiness health-exec and discoveryReplayFixture stop/start/pg_dump stay on plain this.compose(...) (fold-in #2).
- `composeRun(result, label, args, options)` — prepends EXACTLY ['compose','-p',this.id,'-f',this.file] then appends args verbatim. Use the rewrite rule for database-start, migrations, test-migrations, suite, deploy, cleanup down.
- `execSql({service,user,db}, query)` — argv pinned ['exec','-T',service,'psql','-X','-v','ON_ERROR_STOP=1','-U',user,'-d',db,'-At'] with { input: query }. DAD sql(query) becomes `execSql({service:'postgres',user:'atm_owner',db:'dad_atm'}, query)`.

Helpers with a slightly adapted (not 1:1 textual) shape — FEAT-002 should bind config/branching around them:
- `snapshot(result, { requiredFiles, requireMessage, source })` — SNAPSHOT WAS EXTRACTED to base (byte-identity preserved). DAD-specific pieces are injected: requiredFiles = ['apps/donor-api/Dockerfile','apps/web/Dockerfile','apps/web/package-lock.json']; requireMessage = file => `DAD adapter requires ${file}.`; source = this.sourceIdentity ?? this.repo. Everything else (rev-parse 40-64 hex check, .env refusal regex, ls-tree, git archive -> tar -x into this.source, sourceArchiveSha256 via digest, diff-tree/status candidate bookkeeping incl. excludesWorkingTreeChanges:true/workingTreeDirty, candidate.json evidence, the exact summary string) is in the base method unchanged. DAD's snapshot(result) should just `return this.snapshot...`? NO — name clash: the base method IS named `snapshot`. FEAT-002 option: DAD overrides snapshot(result) and calls `super.snapshot(result, { requiredFiles, requireMessage, source })`. That preserves bytes. (If FEAT-002 prefers to avoid super, it may instead keep the full snapshot body in DAD and not use the base method — byte-identity still holds either way; the base method is a convenience.)
- `buildImages(result, builds, inspects)` — generic build+inspect. builds = [{label,args,options}] where args follow 'build' (helper prepends 'build'); inspects = [{service, image}] -> run.data.candidate.images[service]. The mode-conditional *-checks branching (build-${service}-checks, --target build -t ${id}/${service}-checks:local, mode guard) is NOT in this helper — DAD must assemble the resolved `builds` list itself (including the checks entries when mode !== 'exploration') and pass it in, per design §3. NOTE: DAD's current build() interleaves the checks-build and main-build inside a per-service loop and computes shared `args` (label/revision/-f/build-args) per service; FEAT-002 can either (a) build the flat `builds` array first then call buildImages once, or (b) keep DAD's loop calling this.logged directly — whichever keeps the emitted argv element-for-element identical. buildImages is optional convenience, not mandatory.
- `up(result, label, services, {waitTimeout, options})`, `down(result, label, options)` — thin composeRun wrappers. OPTIONAL. Note down() hardcodes ['down','--volumes','--remove-orphans','--timeout','10'] with default { timeout: 90_000 }. database-start uses up -d --wait --wait-timeout 90; deploy uses --wait-timeout 120 + { timeout: 180_000 } — up()'s default waitTimeout is '90', so deploy must pass waitTimeout:'120' and options {timeout:180_000}. Because the exact argv/labels matter for the byte-identical argv guards in FEAT-006, FEAT-002 may prefer calling composeRun directly with the literal REST arrays rather than these wrappers; the wrappers are provided but not required.
- `cleanupFlow(result, { logServices, logLabel, emptyMessage })` — generic cleanup. DAD binds logServices=['api','web','ingress'], logLabel='services' (collected log evidence is 'services.log' in current DAD), emptyMessage='No application environment was created.'. Produces the 'down' composeRun and the no-op cleanup.log. The DAD cleanup summary string stays in DAD. Verify the emitted down argv matches the pinned literal in FEAT-006.

Byte-identity note: snapshot logic was EXTRACTED to base (did NOT stay in DAD) because the extraction is a provable identity — only requiredFiles, the require error-message text, and candidate.source were parameterized; the archive/hash/candidate-bookkeeping bytes are unchanged. If FEAT-006 argv/JSON guards ever flag drift, fall back to keeping snapshot in the DAD subclass.

Import note: base.js imports `{ command } from '../process.js'` and `{ digest, RunError } from '../core.js'` (one level up from src/targets/). From src/targets/dad/index.js, import base as `'../base.js'`.
